limitations: Verified for n = 5..16 and for the products 30, 35, 40, 42, 45, 56, 63, 72; sampling hit rates (about 1/n^2 per random Latin square of the right parity) suggest the number of full-period quasigroups grows like L(n)/n^2, but there is no proof. Plain depth-first search and a SAT encoding stall at n = 9, so random sampling was the only method that scaled.
statement: For every n >= 5 there is a quasigroup of order n whose Fibonacci pair map is a single cycle through all n^2 pairs.
title: Full-period quasigroups exist for every order n >= 5
